rachel: opened a small PR to tighten up SDK examples for streaming + pagination. main asks: show safe teardown, explicit kv-cache hint use, and a tiny test snippet to validate resume behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5340 :memo:

tom: nice. can we add a 1-line test for resume idempotency? support keeps getting questions about duplicate chunks after resume.

yuri: added a short python unit test pattern that asserts no duplicate seq ids when resuming. also clarified naming differences across SDKs (snake_case vs camelCase).

yuri: ```python
# python - unit test sketch for resume idempotency
def test_resume_dedupe(tmp_path):
    client = TestClient()
    # simulate a page stream that fails mid-way
    stream = client.stream('gpt-4o-mini', batch_size=3, kv_cache_hint='doc:xyz')
    consumed = []
    try:
        for chunk in stream:
            consumed.append(chunk.seq)
            if len(consumed) == 2:
                raise TransientError()
    except TransientError:
        # resume using last token and ensure no duplicate seqs
        stream.resume(stream.last_resume_token)
        for chunk in stream:
            consumed.append(chunk.seq)
    assert len(consumed) == len(set(consumed))
```

rachel: perfect, that test snippet will help support. can someone add a tiny TS example showing try/finally close and an inline comment about why small batch_size helps latency?

tom: pushed a TS snippet and a short sentence: "Prefer small batches (3-5) for interactive streams; raise to 8-16 for throughput jobs."

rachel: also found one broken link in pagination guide pointing to old paged-iterators page. i updated it in the PR.

qa-bot: automated preview built: https://deploy-preview-5340--docs.redwood.ai (preview)

yuri: one more nit: in the Go example we used KVCacheHint but the SDK uses kv_cache_hint in docs for consistency. i'll align casing per-language in examples.

tom: sounds good. i'll do a final pass on wording and then request reviews from @yuri and @rachel. thanks all :rocket:
